newsitem.title: USA: Ford's Nasser sees no plant closings.
newsitem.headline: Ford's Nasser sees no plant closings.

text.p: The president of Ford Motor Co.'s automotive operations said Thursday that the company has no plans to close North American assembly plants and described a published report on the subject as "lacking substance."
Jacques Nasser, President of Ford Automotive Operations, told reporters that the nation's second largest automaker was always studying alternatives for its manufacturing facilities.
"But we have no plans and we've made no decisions on plant closings," he said.

Nasser also said Ford also has no plans to reduce capacity for its Explorer compact sport utility vehicle. Nasser noted that the Explorer had strong sales over the last two to three months despite increased competition.
The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that Ford was considering closing its Lorain, Ohio, car plant and consolidating its Explorer production into a single plant, at Louisville, Ky.
Asked about the story, Nasser said, "I view that whole story as surprising and lacking substance."
An industry source, however, said Ford has considered closing the Lorain plant to boost profits in its core North American automotive business.
Under that plan, Ford might build a new, smaller sport utility vehicle previously earmarked for Lorain at a St. Louis plant that also builds Explorers, the source said.

Nasser spoke to reporters at a ceremony at Ford's Wayne, Mich., truck plant, to announce that Ford has become the first major automaker to achieve the industry's top quality certification on a global basis.
